fixer.summary: help_check now refuses any target that game.is_ally doesn't count as the helper's ally (an enemy, for example). The refusal carries page=176 and rule=GLOSS.ally#3. It runs after the R-36 self-check and before the proficiency checks, so nothing is spent and no effect is added. It reuses is_ally (party, team, friendly attitude, GM team designation) rather than adding a second ally test. The ticket test passes with --runxfail. In the normal run its only failure is the strict XPASS, which goes away when the harness removes the marker. Unit tests: 543 passed. Acceptance suites otherwise green. dev-gate: PASS. ruff check and ruff format --check are clean.

review.summary: The fix resolves T-89. `help_check` now refuses any creature that the existing `Game.is_ally` says isn't the helper's ally, so helping an enemy goi is refused and no Advantage is given. The check uses `Game.is_ally` instead of comparing teams again, so friends and GM-designated allies still count. The earlier self-help refusal stays in place because it gives a specific message tied to ruling R-36. Removing the T-89 xfail from the acceptance test is the right move now that the engine behaves correctly. The two new unit tests check real behaviour: helping an enemy is refused, the enemy gets no Advantage effect and nothing is logged; helping a Friendly creature outside the party still works. One small point: the refusal cites `GLOSS.ally#3` ('on your side'), while the acceptance test's marker uses `#4`. That's a defensible choice of clause, not a defect. The other places that still decide 'ally' by comparing teams are already covered by T-93, so I filed no follow-up.
